site.title: PoliteBastART
site.description: Freelance illustrator and street artist based in Croatia. PoliteBastart I Vedran Štimac.

about: After graduating in economics at the Faculty of Economics and Tourism in Pula, I moved to Ljubljana to pursue a PhD in political anthropology, researching peasant social movements. I came close to finishing it, but chose to step away and devote myself fully to art. Those years still shape everything I make.

My whole body of work is rooted in social themes and social problems. Through art – on walls, on paper and on canvas – I try to bring them into public discourse and make room for the stories that history tends to leave out.

I have been working in illustration since 2014, where my main focus has been the portrait: through it I try to convey the ideas and the life of the person portrayed and to build a story behind every image. Alongside illustration I paint murals and make screen prints, and I tattoo as a member of the Jutarnja šetnja tattoo collective in Zagreb. Over the years I have worked for numerous clients, both through illustration and through murals. Since 2025 my focus has shifted to painting: in oil on canvas I explore the everyday lives of ordinary people, most recently in the series Vikendom rekreativno.
I am the co-organiser of Art Park Pula and the organiser of the street art festival Kistom kroz zid in Pula.
exhibitions: Brodac Gallery; Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina
UDAS Gallery; Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina
Open Public University of Poreč, Poreč, Croatia
"Drawing Politics - Drawing of Politics" - Group exhibition
"Drawing Politics - Drawing of Politics" - Group exhibition
International festival of alternative theater PUF - Group exhibition

illustrations.name: Louise Michel
illustrations.caption: 2021, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Louise Michel (1830–1905) was a French teacher, anarchist and one of the most famous figures of the Paris Commune of 1871.
Inside the portrait the Communards rise behind the banner “Vive la Commune”: the uprising she fought for, carried in her head long after its defeat.

illustrations.name: Venedikt Jerofejev
illustrations.caption: 2021, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Venedikt Yerofeyev (1938–1990) was a Soviet writer, best known for the prose poem “Moscow–Petushki”, a drunken train journey through late-Soviet life.
The Kremlin’s onion domes turn into bottles labelled Moscow and Petushki – the beginning and the end of the book’s journey.

illustrations.name: Mercedes Sosa
illustrations.caption: 2021, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Mercedes Sosa (1935–2009) was an Argentine singer, often called the voice of Latin America and of the Nueva Canción movement.
In place of her face is a heart drifting among clouds, watched over by the Sun of May – the songs she sang for the people of the continent.

illustrations.name: Stjepan Filipović
illustrations.caption: 2021, Digital Illustration
text: Stjepan Filipović (1916–1942) was a Yugoslav partisan and People’s Hero. Moments before his execution in Valjevo he raised his arms and called out against fascism – a gesture captured in one of the best-known photographs of the Second World War.
In the portrait his gesture multiplies: people in the streets and windows raise their arms with him.

illustrations.name: Diego Armando Maradona
illustrations.caption: 2021, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Diego Armando Maradona (1960–2020) was an Argentine footballer and one of the greatest players of all time.
The “Hand of God” rises with the ball as a halo, a stairway leads through it towards a red star – the street kid who climbed to the sky of world football.

illustrations.name: Nikola Tesla
illustrations.caption: 2015, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Nikola Tesla (1856–1943) was an inventor and engineer whose work on alternating current shaped the modern world.
His greatest inventions are drawn as one intricate mechanism inside his head, based on original vintage engineering plans. Hand-drawn dotwork, about 30–40 hours of work.

illustrations.name: Yevgeny Zamyatin
illustrations.caption: 2017, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Yevgeny Zamyatin (1884–1937) was a Russian writer whose novel “We” is one of the first great dystopias of the 20th century.
A glass cell closes around an eye and the globe – the transparent houses of the One State, where every citizen is always watched.

illustrations.name: Galileo Galilei
illustrations.caption: 2015, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Galileo Galilei (1564–1642) was an astronomer and physicist, often called the father of modern science.
Inside his head are the heliocentric model he defended and the Leaning Tower of Pisa – his birthplace and the setting of his legendary experiments with gravity.

illustrations.name: Quentin Tarantino
illustrations.caption: 2020, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Quentin Tarantino (b. 1963) is an American film director and screenwriter.
His face breaks into sharp geometric shards in the warm, saturated colours of his films, with a splash of blood on the collar.

illustrations.name: Simon Bolivar
illustrations.caption: 2018, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Simón Bolívar (1783–1830), “El Libertador”, led the independence struggles of much of South America against Spanish rule.
The map of South America becomes a fist gripping a musket – a continent taking its freedom into its own hands.

illustrations.name: Karlo Rojc
illustrations.caption: 2015, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Karlo Rojc was a Yugoslav national hero from Pula whose life spanned two world wars. After the First World War he served as an officer aboard the submarine Smeli, symbolised in the portrait by an hourglass – fleeting time and a lasting legacy.
The former army barracks in Pula named after him is today the Rojc social centre, home to music and art collectives.

illustrations.name: Karl Marx
illustrations.caption: 2020, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Karl Marx (1818–1883) was a philosopher, economist and author of “The Communist Manifesto” and “Capital”.
Inside the portrait is the world he wrote about: the city, the workers and their struggle for equality. Hand-drawn dotwork.

illustrations.name: Milja Marin
illustrations.caption: 2015, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Milja Marin was a Yugoslav partisan whose wartime portrait became one of the iconic images of women in the antifascist struggle.
Under the partisan cap with a red star her face is broken into geometric shapes, with a rifle over her shoulder.

illustrations.name: Herman Melville
illustrations.caption: 2015, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Herman Melville (1819–1891) was an American novelist, author of “Moby-Dick”.

The whale fills his silhouette and its eye replaces his own – the line between creator and creation disappears. Captain Ahab stands with his harpoon, and two card suits float in the sea: luck shapes the fate of even the most determined.

illustrations.name: Franz Kafka
illustrations.caption: 2015, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Franz Kafka (1883–1924) was a writer from Prague, author of “The Metamorphosis” and “The Trial”.
Like the other portraits in the series, his work is drawn on his face: insects and human figures echo Gregor Samsa’s transformation. Dotwork, about 30–40 hours of work.

illustrations.name: Ivica Vidović
illustrations.caption: 2020, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Ivica Vidović (1939–2011) was a Croatian actor, remembered as Servantes in the series “Naše malo misto” – the dreamer who returns from Chile to a small Dalmatian town to translate Don Quixote.
The portrait captures the character’s grotesque heroism and quiet dignity: idealism, art and quiet rebellion.

illustrations.name: Alfred Hitchcock
illustrations.caption: 2016, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Alfred Hitchcock (1899–1980) was a film director known as the master of suspense.
Inside his famous silhouette are scenes from three of his films – Vertigo, Rear Window and The Birds.

illustrations.name: Ernest Hemingway
illustrations.caption: 2015, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Ernest Hemingway (1899–1961) was an American writer and Nobel Prize laureate.
Half of his face opens into the sea of “The Old Man and the Sea”: the old fisherman in his boat, the great marlin and the sun over the water.

illustrations.name: Fidel Castro
illustrations.caption: 2017, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Fidel Castro (1926–2016) was the leader of the Cuban Revolution.

The portrait is built from symbols of the revolution, including the Moncada Barracks, where the movement began in 1953. Above it stands his line that a revolution is not a bed of roses, but a struggle between the future and the past.

illustrations.name: M.C. Escher
illustrations.caption: 2018, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: M. C. Escher (1898–1972) was a Dutch graphic artist known for impossible constructions and endless tessellations.
His face dissolves into interlocking fish, in the spirit of his own transforming patterns.

illustrations.name: Edgar Allan Poe
illustrations.caption: 2016, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Edgar Allan Poe (1809–1849) was an American writer and poet, master of the macabre.
The raven sits on his brow next to a pale woman’s face – the lost Lenore of his most famous poem.

illustrations.name: Che Guevara
illustrations.caption: 2020, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Ernesto “Che” Guevara (1928–1967) was a revolutionary and one of the leaders of the Cuban Revolution.

Inside his head are factory chimneys and a worker and a farmer who together bring down the beast of capital – a picture of class struggle and solidarity. Hand-drawn dotwork, about 30–40 hours of work.

illustrations.name: Miguel de Cervantes
illustrations.caption: 2016, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Miguel de Cervantes (1547–1616) was a Spanish writer, author of “Don Quixote”.
Don Quixote charges with his lance again – this time not at windmills, but at smoking factory chimneys.

illustrations.name: Albert Camus
illustrations.caption: 2016, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Albert Camus (1913–1960) was a French writer and philosopher of the absurd, author of “The Myth of Sisyphus”.
A chain ties him to the boulder Sisyphus pushes uphill. Once Sisyphus accepts the absurdity of life, the task becomes lighter and the burden is shared.

illustrations.name: Vladimir Nabokov
illustrations.caption: 2015, Ink on paper; Digitally colored
text: Vladimir Nabokov (1899–1977) was a Russian-American novelist and a passionate lepidopterist.
A butterfly sits on his forehead among fragments and objects from his novels, assembled like a collector’s case.

street_art.name: Mural "Imagine the Better World"
street_art.caption: Pula, Croatia (2025)
text: Painted on the façade of Vidikovac Primary School in Pula, the mural shows a pupil striding forward towards a better future, one shaped by peace, solidarity and prosperity.
Holding the globe close and setting a white dove free, the figure carries the world with care into the time ahead.

hr.name: Mural „Imagine the Better World“
hr.caption: Pula, Hrvatska (2025)
text: Mural na pročelju Osnovne škole Vidikovac u Puli prikazuje učenika koji korača prema boljoj budućnosti – budućnosti određenoj mirom, solidarnošću i prosperitetom.
Držeći globus uz sebe i puštajući bijelu golubicu, lik s pažnjom nosi svijet u vrijeme koje dolazi.

street_art.name: Mural of Vladimir Nazor
street_art.caption: Pazin, Croatia (2025)
text: Vladimir Nazor (1876–1949) was one of the most important Croatian poets and writers. His story “Veli Jože” – about a gentle giant from Motovun who breaks free from his masters – became a symbol of the Istrian people and their struggle for freedom.

The mural was painted on the façade of Vladimir Nazor Primary School in Pazin, during six days in the sun. Inside the portrait is Veli Jože carrying a sheaf of wheat past a hilltop Istrian town, and women harvesting in the fields – the land and the people Nazor wrote about.

hr.name: Mural Vladimir Nazor
hr.caption: Pazin, Hrvatska (2025)
text: Vladimir Nazor (1876. – 1949.) jedan je od najvažnijih hrvatskih pjesnika i pisaca. Njegova pripovijest „Veli Jože“ – o dobroćudnom divu iz Motovuna koji se oslobađa svojih gospodara – postala je simbol istarskog naroda i njegove borbe za slobodu.

Mural je naslikan na pročelju Osnovne škole Vladimira Nazora u Pazinu, kroz šest dana na suncu. Unutar portreta je Veli Jože koji nosi snop žita pokraj istarskog gradića na brežuljku i žene koje žanju u polju – zemlja i ljudi o kojima je Nazor pisao.

street_art.name: Mural of Frida Kahlo
street_art.caption: Zagreb, Croatia (2024)
text: Frida Kahlo (1907–1954) was a Mexican painter, known for her self-portraits, her bold use of colour and the symbols of Mexican folk culture.

The mural, painted at Studio-galerija Klet in Zagreb, is based on my illustration of her. A bird spreads its wings across her face, leaves grow on her cheeks and flowers crown her hair, all set against a sun-like halo.

hr.name: Mural Frida Kahlo
hr.caption: Zagreb, Hrvatska (2024)
text: Frida Kahlo (1907. – 1954.) bila je meksička slikarica, poznata po autoportretima, hrabrim bojama i simbolima meksičke narodne kulture.

Mural, naslikan u Studio-galeriji Klet u Zagrebu, nastao je prema mojoj ilustraciji. Ptica širi krila preko njezina lica, na obrazima rastu listovi, a kosu krune cvjetovi – sve ispred aureole nalik suncu.

street_art.name: Mural of Karlo Rojc
street_art.caption: Pula, Croatia (2023)
text: Karlo Rojc was a national hero from Pula. The former army barracks named after him is today the Karlo Rojc community centre, home to dozens of associations, music and art collectives.

The mural was painted on the centre's building during the Kistom kroz zid street art festival. Inside the portrait are the submarine and the hourglass from my illustration of Rojc, together with the façade of the building that carries his name.

hr.name: Mural Karlo Rojc
hr.caption: Pula, Hrvatska (2023)
text: Karlo Rojc bio je narodni heroj iz Pule. Bivša vojarna koja nosi njegovo ime danas je Društveni centar Karlo Rojc, dom desetaka udruga te glazbenih i umjetničkih kolektiva.

Mural je naslikan na zgradi centra tijekom festivala ulične umjetnosti Kistom kroz zid. Unutar portreta su podmornica i pješčani sat s moje ilustracije Rojca, zajedno s pročeljem zgrade koja nosi njegovo ime.

street_art.name: Mural of Julije Knifer
street_art.caption: Zagreb, Croatia (2021)
text: Julije Knifer (23 April 1924 – 7 December 2004) was a Croatian abstract painter and a founding member of the Gorgona Group, a Croatian art collective of the 1960s.
The central motif of the mural is Knifer's meander, a geometric form he created from 1960 onwards in various techniques such as print, oil, acrylic and collage.

hr.name: Mural Julije Knifer
hr.caption: Zagreb, Hrvatska (2021)
text: Julije Knifer (23. travnja 1924. – 7. prosinca 2004.) bio je hrvatski apstraktni slikar i jedan od osnivača Gorgone, hrvatskog umjetničkog kolektiva iz 1960-ih.
Središnji motiv murala je Kniferov meandar, geometrijski oblik koji je od 1960. stvarao u različitim tehnikama – grafici, ulju, akrilu i kolažu.

street_art.name: Mural of Antonio Gauchito Gil
street_art.caption: Zagreb, Croatia (2021)
text: Antonio Gauchito Gil was an Argentine "Robin Hood" who lived as an outlaw in the 1800s after refusing to fight in a civil war. Stealing from the rich and giving to the poor, the legendary outlaw became a folk saint. Today Gauchito is revered as a „people's saint“, protector of the poor, the oppressed and everyone living on the margins of society.
The portrait contains candles, often found at his roadside shrines, and a medallion of San La Muerte. Legend says the medallion saved him from a bullet and certain death.

hr.name: Mural Antonio Gauchito Gil
hr.caption: Zagreb, Hrvatska (2021)
text: Antonio Gauchito Gil bio je argentinski „Robin Hood“ koji je u 19. stoljeću živio kao odmetnik nakon što je odbio ratovati u građanskom ratu. Kradući od bogatih i dajući siromašnima, legendarni odmetnik postao je narodni svetac. Gauchita i danas štuju kao „svetca naroda“, zaštitnika siromašnih, potlačenih i svih koji žive na margini društva.
U portretu su svijeće, kakve se često nalaze uz njegova svetišta uz cestu, i medaljon San La Muerte. Legenda kaže da ga je upravo taj medaljon spasio od metka i sigurne smrti.

street_art.name: Mural of Rossana Rossanda
street_art.caption: Pula, Croatia (2021)
text: Rossana Rossanda (1924–2020) was born in Pula, Croatia, during the early consolidation of Benito Mussolini's Fascist regime. She was a journalist, writer, feminist and a leading figure in Italian politics. She took part in the partisan movement, was a militant member of the PCI (from which she was expelled for her criticism of Soviet authoritarianism) and sat in the Italian parliament from 1963 to 1968. She was one of the founders of the influential paper „il manifesto“, which remained the most critical daily in Berlusconi's Italy.

The main motif of the mural is her departure from this world: she climbs the stairs into a more just world – the world she fought for all her life. The curtains are made of pages of „il manifesto“, the paper she co-founded and edited.

hr.name: Mural Rossana Rossanda
hr.caption: Pula, Hrvatska (2021)
text: Rossana Rossanda (1924. – 2020.) rođena je u Puli u vrijeme učvršćivanja fašističkog režima Benita Mussolinija. Bila je novinarka, spisateljica, feministkinja i jedna od ključnih figura talijanske politike. Sudjelovala je u partizanskom pokretu, bila militantna članica Komunističke partije Italije (iz koje je izbačena zbog kritike sovjetskog autoritarizma) i zastupnica u talijanskom parlamentu od 1963. do 1968. Jedna je od osnivačica utjecajnog lista „il manifesto“, koji je ostao najkritičniji dnevnik Berlusconijeve Italije.

Glavni motiv murala je njezin odlazak s ovoga svijeta: penje se stepenicama u pravedniji svijet – svijet za koji se borila cijeli život. Zavjese su napravljene od stranica „il manifesta“, lista koji je suosnovala i uređivala.

street_art.name: Mural of "Solidarity with The People of Palestine"
street_art.caption: Sisak, Croatia (2021)
text: For decades the State of Israel has carried out systematic oppression and ethnic cleansing of the Palestinian population: land grabs, forced displacement, cuts to electricity and water supplies, blockades of goods and services (for example, a ban on importing Covid vaccines for medical staff), and the bombing of the Gaza Strip, where in 2021 alone 256 people were killed, among them 66 children and 40 women. In the face of injustice it is important not to stay silent, because silence means standing on the side of the oppressor.

The mural was painted on a residential building in Sisak as a call to end Israeli aggression, as solidarity with the people of Palestine, and as a hope for a brighter, more peaceful and freer future for everyone in Palestine and Israel who suffers violence and daily injustice. The silhouette of the portrait belongs to Leila Khaled, Palestinian activist and intellectual.

hr.name: Mural „Solidarity with The People of Palestine“
hr.caption: Sisak, Hrvatska (2021)
text: Država Izrael desetljećima provodi sustavno ugnjetavanje i etničko čišćenje palestinskog stanovništva: otimanje zemlje, prisilna preseljenja, prekide opskrbe strujom i vodom, blokade robe i usluga (primjerice zabranu uvoza cjepiva protiv covida za medicinsko osoblje) te bombardiranje Pojasa Gaze, u kojem je samo 2021. ubijeno 256 ljudi, od toga 66 djece i 40 žena. Kad se događa nepravda, važno je ne šutjeti, jer šutnjom stajemo na stranu tlačitelja.

Mural je naslikan na stambenoj zgradi u Sisku kao poziv na prestanak izraelske agresije, kao solidarnost s narodom Palestine i kao nada u svjetliju, mirniju i slobodniju budućnost za sve u Palestini i Izraelu koji trpe nasilje i svakodnevnu nepravdu. Silueta portreta pripada Leili Khaled, palestinskoj aktivistici i intelektualki.

street_art.name: Mural of "Solidarity with Rojava Revolution"
street_art.caption: Pula, Croatia (2020)
text: The Rojava Revolution is a political upheaval and military conflict in northern Syria, known among Kurds as Western Kurdistan or Rojava. A new kind of society is being built there: surrounded by ISIS and hostile Turkish forces, the people of the Rojava cantons are creating one of the most radically progressive societies on the planet today.

The dominant colours of the mural – red, green and yellow – are the colours of Rojava's flag. The three female portraits symbolise solidarity among the women of Syria and feminism, the cornerstone of Rojava's democratic confederalism.

hr.name: Mural „Solidarity with Rojava Revolution“
hr.caption: Pula, Hrvatska (2020)
text: Revolucija u Rojavi politički je preokret i vojni sukob na sjeveru Sirije, području koje Kurdi nazivaju Zapadnim Kurdistanom ili Rojavom. Ondje se gradi nova vrsta društva: okruženi ISIL-om i neprijateljskim turskim snagama, stanovnici kantona Rojave stvaraju jedno od najradikalnije progresivnih društava na planetu.
Dominantne boje murala – crvena, zelena i žuta – boje su zastave Rojave. Tri ženska portreta simboliziraju solidarnost među ženama Sirije i feminizam, temelj demokratskog konfederalizma Rojave.

street_art.name: Mural of "Fallen Industry"
street_art.caption: Pula, Croatia (2020)
text: Twenty years ago Pula was an industrial city. The shipyard and various factories provided a decent living for half of the city's population. Today deindustrialisation and an economy based solely on tourism are devastating the welfare of Pula's citizens.

The piece is dedicated to the Uljanik shipyard, one of the last bastions of Pula's industry. The continuous sell-off of public goods to private interests pushes many of us into existential crisis. The modified Louis Vuitton pattern presents the shipyard as a pure commodity for sale.

hr.name: Mural „Fallen Industry“
hr.caption: Pula, Hrvatska (2020)
text: Prije dvadesetak godina Pula je bila industrijski grad. Brodogradilište i brojne tvornice osiguravale su pristojan život polovici stanovnika. Danas deindustrijalizacija i gospodarstvo oslonjeno samo na turizam razaraju dobrobit građana Pule.

Rad je posvećen brodogradilištu Uljanik, jednom od posljednjih bastiona pulske industrije. Neprekidna rasprodaja javnih dobara u korist privatnih interesa mnoge od nas gura u egzistencijalnu krizu. Izmijenjeni uzorak Louis Vuittona prikazuje brodogradilište kao čistu robu na prodaju.

street_art.name: Mural of "Latinoamerica Lucha"
street_art.caption: Buenos Aires, Argentina (2019)
text: In 2019 Chile saw huge mass demonstrations against neoliberal policies. Protests spread across the country in response to a rise in Santiago Metro fares, the increasing cost of living, privatisation and the inequality prevalent in the country.

The mural was painted on the former prison in the Barracas neighbourhood of Buenos Aires. The silhouette of the portrait belongs to a native Latin American woman. Inside it is a woman with the flag of the Mapuche people (the native people who suffered most under colonial rule) and the Wiphala – a square emblem used as a flag by native peoples of the Andes, in today's Peru, Bolivia and parts of Ecuador, Argentina, Chile and Colombia.

hr.name: Mural „Latinoamerica Lucha“
hr.caption: Buenos Aires, Argentina (2019)
text: Čile je 2019. godine potresli masovni prosvjedi protiv neoliberalnih politika. Prosvjedi su se proširili zemljom kao odgovor na poskupljenje karata za podzemnu željeznicu u Santiagu, rast troškova života, privatizaciju i duboku nejednakost.

Mural je naslikan na bivšem zatvoru u četvrti Barracas u Buenos Airesu. Silueta portreta pripada domorotkinji Latinske Amerike. Unutar nje je žena sa zastavom naroda Mapuche (domorodačkog naroda koji je najviše stradao pod kolonijalnom vlašću) i Wiphalom – četvrtastim znakom koji kao zastavu koriste domorodački narodi Anda, na području današnjeg Perua, Bolivije te dijelova Ekvadora, Argentine, Čilea i Kolumbije.

street_art.name: Mural of "Cities for People, Not for Profit"
street_art.caption: Ljubljana, Slovenia (2019)
text: Gentrification and rising rents driven by the free market affect huge numbers of people. Even in the so-called „developed“ West, many cannot afford decent housing. Young people still live with their parents, the „lucky“ ones share flats with two or more roommates, and many cannot afford even that and end up homeless.

Inside the portrait is a map of Ljubljana centred on AKC Metelkova, with a keyhole painted on it. The rat symbolises the marginalised, oppressed and stigmatised citizens who hold the "key" to their city. The only question is when they will use that "key" to fight urban planning driven by profit.

hr.name: Mural „Cities for People, Not for Profit“
hr.caption: Ljubljana, Slovenija (2019)
text: Gentrifikacija i rast najamnina potaknuti slobodnim tržištem pogađaju golem broj ljudi. Čak i na takozvanom „razvijenom“ Zapadu mnogi si ne mogu priuštiti pristojan stan. Mladi i dalje žive s roditeljima, „sretnici“ dijele stan s dvoje ili više cimera, a mnogi si ne mogu priuštiti ni to i završe bez krova nad glavom.

Unutar portreta je karta Ljubljane sa središtem na AKC Metelkova, na kojoj je nacrtana ključanica. Štakor simbolizira marginalizirane, potlačene i stigmatizirane građane koji drže „ključ“ svoga grada. Pitanje je samo trenutka kada će taj „ključ“ upotrijebiti i suprotstaviti se urbanizmu vođenom logikom profita.

street_art.name: Mural of Herbert Marcuse
street_art.caption: Krapina, Croatia (2017)
text: Herbert Marcuse was a German-American philosopher, sociologist and political theorist associated with the Frankfurt School of critical theory. In his best-known book, „One-Dimensional Man“, he argues that whether we are workers or bureaucrats, we are all victims of consumer society.
The background of the portrait is a barcode, a symbol of consumer society, and inside the portrait are white- and blue-collar workers – the central idea of „One-Dimensional Man“.

hr.name: Mural Herbert Marcuse
hr.caption: Krapina, Hrvatska (2017)
text: Herbert Marcuse bio je njemačko-američki filozof, sociolog i politički teoretičar, povezan s Frankfurtskom školom kritičke teorije. U svojoj najpoznatijoj knjizi „Jednodimenzionalni čovjek“ tvrdi da smo, bili radnici ili birokrati, svi zajedno žrtve potrošačkog društva.
Pozadina portreta je bar-kod, simbol potrošačkog društva, a unutar portreta su radnici u plavim i bijelim ovratnicima – središnja ideja „Jednodimenzionalnog čovjeka“.

street_art.name: Mural of Sean Connery
street_art.caption: Umag, Croatia (2016)
text: Sir Sean Connery was a Scottish actor and the first to play the British secret agent James Bond on film, starring in seven Bond films between 1962 and 1983.
The portrait shows him in „From Russia with Love“. In place of his face is the famous gun-barrel opening sequence of the James Bond films.

hr.name: Mural Sean Connery
hr.caption: Umag, Hrvatska (2016)
text: Sir Sean Connery bio je škotski glumac i prvi filmski James Bond, britanski tajni agent kojeg je utjelovio u sedam filmova između 1962. i 1983.
Portret ga prikazuje u filmu „Iz Rusije s ljubavlju“. Umjesto lica je slavna uvodna scena filmova o Jamesu Bondu, pogled kroz cijev pištolja.

street_art.name: Mural of Dragutin Gorjanović Kramberger
street_art.caption: Krapina, Croatia (2015)
text: Dragutin Gorjanović-Kramberger was a Croatian geologist, palaeontologist and archaeologist. His most famous discovery is the Neanderthal skull „type C“ from Hušnjak Hill near Krapina.
In this piece the Neanderthal skull „type C“ appears as a mask on Gorjanović's face. The mural was painted in Krapina because of the heritage his work left to the town.

hr.name: Mural Dragutin Gorjanović Kramberger
hr.caption: Krapina, Hrvatska (2015)
text: Dragutin Gorjanović-Kramberger bio je hrvatski geolog, paleontolog i arheolog. Njegovo najpoznatije otkriće je neandertalska lubanja „tip C“ s brda Hušnjakovo kraj Krapine.
Na ovom radu neandertalska lubanja „tip C“ pojavljuje se kao maska na Gorjanovićevu licu. Mural je naslikan u Krapini zbog nasljeđa koje je njegov rad ostavio gradu.

about_hr: Nakon diplome na Fakultetu ekonomije i turizma u Puli preselio sam se u Ljubljanu, gdje sam upisao doktorski studij političke antropologije i istraživao seljačke društvene pokrete. Bio sam blizu kraja, ali sam odlučio odustati i posvetiti se u potpunosti umjetnosti. Te godine i danas oblikuju sve što radim.

Cijeli moj opus temelji se na društvenim temama i društvenim problemima. Kroz umjetnost – na zidu, na papiru i na platnu – nastojim ih unijeti u javni diskurs i otvoriti prostor za priče koje povijest često izostavlja.

Ilustracijom se bavim od 2014. godine, a u njoj mi je glavni fokus portret: kroz njega nastojim prenijeti ideje i život osobe koju prikazujem i izgraditi priču iza svake slike. Uz ilustraciju slikam murale i radim sitotisak, a tetoviram kao član tattoo kolektiva Jutarnja šetnja u Zagrebu. Tijekom godina radio sam za brojne klijente, kroz ilustraciju i kroz murale. Od 2025. fokus sam prebacio na slikarstvo: uljem na platnu istražujem svakodnevicu običnih ljudi, posljednje u ciklusu Vikendom rekreativno.
Suorganizator sam Art Parka Pula i organizator festivala ulične umjetnosti Kistom kroz zid u Puli.

paintings.title: Vikendom rekreativno
text_hr: Vikend u suvremenoj svakodnevnici gotovo redovno promatram kao svojevrstan rascjep u kontinuitetu života. Pridajemo mu gotovo mitski značaj: doživljavamo ga kao privremenu autonomnu zonu, obećanje odmaka od rutine i mogućnost predaha. U svijetu u kojem je teško zamisliti budućnost onkraj postojećih struktura, osjećaj mogućnosti premješta se u kratke pukotine svakodnevnice, u trenutke kada se javlja slutnja da možemo zastati.

Tijelo je kroz tjedan određeno funkcijom utjelovljenom u radu i vremenu koje prodajemo za nadnicu. Vikendom taj odnos prividno popušta. Tijelo se privremeno izmiče svojoj radnoj ulozi i ponovno pokušava osjetiti vlastitu prisutnost, najčešće kroz melankoliju predaha.

U svojim radovima, nadahnut Hegedušićem i Trumbetašom s jedne strane te Riverom i latinoameričkim socijalnim slikarstvom s druge, kroz prizmu magičnog realizma spojenog s naivnim izričajem postavljam likove i scene unutar vikend-svakodnevnice koja djeluje istovremeno poznato i blago izmješteno.

Moji protagonisti nisu romantizirani heroji radničke klase niti nositelji dociranja o socijalnoj nepravdi, nego obični ljudi zatečeni u trenutku pokušaja da ponovno osjete sebe. Stilski ne djeluju kao akademski ideali; njihova anatomija nije ružna, nego poštena. To su teška i nezgrapno naslikana tijela koja nose tragove svakodnevnice.

Magični realizam ovdje nije prisutan samo kao estetski ukras, nego kao konceptualni alat. Omogućuje mi prikaz vikenda kao blago pomaknutog stanja stvarnosti, vremenske heterotopije u kojoj svakodnevica ostaje prepoznatljiva, ali se otvara prostor emotivnog otklona. To je prostor u kojem sanjamo cigarete dugačke deset metara, u kojem sekunde udaraju srčano, a melankolija sitnih sati vraća nas u polusvijet između sna i navike.
U tom pomaku banalne situacije dobivaju mitsku težinu. Vikend se pojavljuje kao vrijeme u kojem se svakodnevne geste pune očekivanjem da će život barem na trenutak postati gušći i stvarniji.
text_en: In contemporary everyday life I almost always see the weekend as a kind of rupture in the continuity of life. We give it an almost mythical meaning: we experience it as a temporary autonomous zone, a promise of distance from routine and a chance to catch our breath. In a world where it is hard to imagine a future beyond existing structures, the sense of possibility moves into the short cracks of the everyday – into moments when we sense that we might be able to pause.

During the week the body is defined by its function, embodied in work and in the time we sell for a wage. At the weekend this relationship seems to loosen. The body temporarily slips out of its working role and tries once again to feel its own presence, most often through the melancholy of rest.

Inspired by Hegedušić and Trumbetaš on one side, and by Rivera and Latin American social painting on the other, I place my figures and scenes, through the lens of magical realism combined with a naive idiom, within a weekend everyday that feels at once familiar and slightly displaced.

My protagonists are neither romanticised working-class heroes nor vehicles for lectures about social injustice, but ordinary people caught in the moment of trying to feel themselves again. Stylistically they are not academic ideals; their anatomy is not ugly but honest. These are heavy, clumsily painted bodies that carry the traces of everyday life.

Magical realism here is not merely an aesthetic ornament but a conceptual tool. It lets me show the weekend as a slightly shifted state of reality, a temporal heterotopia in which the everyday remains recognisable while a space of emotional detachment opens up. It is a space where we dream of ten-metre-long cigarettes, where seconds beat like a heart, and where the melancholy of the small hours returns us to a half-world between sleep and habit.

In this shift, banal situations acquire mythical weight. The weekend appears as a time when everyday gestures are filled with the expectation that life, at least for a moment, will become denser and more real.
